title: Imperfect and present perfect: how things have changed

sections.content: You know the contrast between the *imperfecto* (imperfect) and the *pretérito perfecto* (present perfect) for change over time from B1 Unit 5. The imperfect describes how things used to be (*antes, las víctimas no hablaban*). The present perfect describes what has changed up to now (*hoy muchas han hablado*). Memory and justice are about exactly this: what was true under the dictatorships and what has happened since.

items.spanish: Antes, muchas víctimas no hablaban de lo que pasaba.
items.english: Before, many victims did not talk about what was happening.

items.spanish: Con los años, muchas han dado su testimonio.
items.english: Over the years, many have given their testimony.

items.spanish: Antes, los jefes militares no eran juzgados; desde 2003 se han reabierto muchos juicios.
items.english: Before, military leaders were not tried; since 2003 many trials have been reopened.

items.spanish: Antes, el pasado era un tema prohibido; hoy se ha convertido en un tema de debate.
items.english: Before, the past was a forbidden subject; today it has become a subject of debate.

sections.content: Time words help you choose. *Antes* and *durante la dictadura* point to the imperfect. *Hoy*, *desde 2003* and *con los años* point to the present perfect, because the change still matters now.
